LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_ReplaceRendererTip: Turn this off to go back to Atmosphere Overhaul's original streamlines and compare.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_AOButtonHint: Atmosphere Overhaul's own streamline button still shows and hides the layer.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_ShowGuideLineTip: Only applies to comet and fine streamlines; particle trails have no baseline.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_SmoothFieldTip: Removes the kinks where streamlines cross cell edges, for a cleaner flow. Affects only comet and fine streamlines; particle trails are unchanged. Turn it off to see AO's raw field.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_DensityTip: How many streamlines or particles appear on screen at once.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_SpeedLengthInfluenceTi: Particle trails only. 1 = stronger wind makes longer trails; lower values bring slow-wind trails closer to the fast-wind length; 0 = all trails the same length. Comet and fine streamlines use "Streamline length" instead.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_LowWindThresholdTip: Particle trails only. Particles slower than this fade out gently instead of popping; higher values keep particles only where the wind is strong. 0 = never hide.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_ColoredParticlesTip: When off, all particles are white.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_SixtyFpsTip: Keeps streamline motion in step with your screen, for smoother movement. Turning it off saves a little performance, but the motion may look like it pauses every other frame on high-refresh displays.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_PauseWhenPaused: Pause streamlines when the game is paused
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_PauseWhenPausedTip: Stops streamline and particle motion while the game is paused; panning or zooming during a pause still fills in particles.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_ScaleSpeedWithGameSpee: Streamlines and particles speed up with game speed, up to 4x. Pause behavior is controlled separately by the item above.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Wind_GpuParticlesTip: Lets the graphics card build the particle trails, taking load off the processor. Looks the same as the normal mode; if your graphics card or driver can't handle it, the game switches back automatically. Uncheck to compare performance.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_ReplaceAOSprites: Use the new gas rendering (replace AO)
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_ReplaceVanillaSprites: Use the new gas rendering (replace vanilla)
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_ReplaceTipWithAO: Replaces mist and the four vanilla gases (blind smoke, tox gas, rot stink, deadlife dust) with a softer, continuous cloud look. Turn it off to restore the original rendering for comparison.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_ReplaceTipVanilla: Replaces the four vanilla gases (blind smoke, tox gas, rot stink, deadlife dust) with a softer, continuous cloud look. Turn it off to restore the original rendering for comparison.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_ShaderMissing: The custom shader failed to load, so this option has no effect (see the log for details).
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_LocalFlow: Gas drifts with the local wind
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_LocalFlowTip: When on, the gas drift pattern follows the nearby wind for a more natural flow; the gust from an explosion is smoothed out so it never jitters back and forth. Turn it off to drift with the global wind instead, for comparison.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_SmoothTip: Makes gas appear, fade and change density smoothly instead of stepping. When off, the gas reacts faster but may show slight stepping.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_SmoothTauTip: Lower values react faster, higher values are softer. It only smooths large density changes, so small adjustments are usually enough.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_AnimationTipWithAO: How fast the gas pattern moves and changes. 0 = pattern stands still (the gas itself still drifts with the wind); 1 = default speed.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_AnimationTipVanilla: How fast the gas pattern drifts with the wind. 0 = pattern stands still (the gas itself still drifts with the wind); 1 = default speed.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_ScaleTip: Smaller values give finer, more broken-up smoke; larger values look like big dense clouds.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_BlurTip: Softens the gas edges, including thin gas. 0 = edges follow the cells; higher values blur the edges more. More blur weakens sharpness.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_SharpenTip: Makes the gas edges crisper and the outline clearer. 0 = the original soft transition; 1 = visibly harder edges. It cancels out against Blur, so more blur means less effect.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_FaintTip: How visible thin gas is. Higher values make faint smoke more obvious; 0 = only thick gas shows; 1 = default.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_OpacityTip: Overall density. Higher values look like heavy smoke rather than thin mist.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_CloudyTip: Adds a clumpy texture over the smooth mist for a smoke feel closer to vanilla. Off gives pure smooth mist.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_ReplaceDeadlifeTip: On: deadlife dust is shaded by the smooth gas field like every other gas, as a navy cloud. Off: the field drops the dust channel and the dust is drawn per cell with vanilla's own sprite texture, keeping its grainy look.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_TraceWindowsTip: Only takes effect in dev mode. For troubleshooting only; when on, it keeps writing to the log and hurts performance.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Gas_DiagnosticsTip: When on, records a full gas-layer snapshot every frame to VisualTweaks_GasField_Flash.log in the system temp folder; this costs performance. To investigate a whole-layer flash while moving the camera, reproduce with it on and then compare with it off. When off, no data is collected at all. Keep it off after testing.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Ripple_EnableTip: Adds an expanding ring of compressed air to every visual explosion: it gently bends the ground and the explosion's own fireball, then fades out near the edge of the blast. Size, strength and duration follow the explosion's radius; the sliders below set the overall look.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Ripple_ShaderMissing: The shockwave shader failed to load, so this option has no effect (see the log for details).
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Ripple_IntensityTip: How strong the shockwave looks, controlling how much the scene bends plus a faint bright crest. Bigger explosions get extra strength from the "bigger blasts are stronger" option.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Ripple_RadiusScaleTip: Multiplies the explosion radius to get the largest shockwave size. 1 = it reaches the damage radius; above 1 it spreads beyond the blast.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Ripple_RadiusInfluenceTip: 0 = every explosion has the same strength; 1 = the bigger the blast, the stronger the shockwave. The default 0.35 makes large blasts more impressive without overpowering small ones.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Ripple_DurationTip: How long the shockwave lasts. The default is 0.5 s, adjustable from about 0.05 s to 2 s. Larger explosions last up to about 1.5 times longer; the effect also finishes sooner when the game is running fast.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldLarge_EnableTip: Redraws projector domes with a shader; turn it off to restore the stock drawing for large shields.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldPersonal_EnableTip: Redraws personal shield belts with a shader; turn it off to restore the stock drawing for belts.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldRepulsor_EnableTip: Redraws the VEF Field Shield, using the large-shield settings below for their look. Hidden when the required mods are not loaded.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldRepulsor_OpacityTip: Overall opacity of repulsor shields. 1.0 is the default; lower values are more see-through.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldBubble_EnableTip: Redraws VEF's pawn shield bubbles (warcasket armour, creature shields, ...) using the personal-shield settings below. Hidden when VEF is not loaded.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldHediff_EnableTip: Redraws shields granted by VEF hediffs or abilities (such as Vanilla Psycasts Expanded's fire shield) using the personal-shield settings below. Hidden when VEF is not loaded.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_OffNote: All shield types use the stock drawing; style settings are inactive.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldAlways_EnableTip: Keeps active large shields faintly visible when not selected. Personal belts still follow vanilla's visibility rules.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Shield_PauseWhenPaused: Pause shield animation when the game is paused
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Shield_PauseWhenPausedTip: Freezes the shield surface's scan and drift, plus vanilla's always-show breathing alpha, while the game is paused. Turn it off to keep them playing. Hit and break animations already follow game time and pause either way.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldOverride_EnableTip: When on, every pawn and building that owns a shield shows a gizmo that opens a style window for this mod's shield. Changes there apply to that object only; any row left on "Follow global" keeps following this page. On by default; the same switch is available inside the style window.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldOverride_GizmoTip: Opens this shield's style settings. Only this pawn or building is affected; rows left on "Follow global" still use the Shields tab. The window also contains the switch that controls whether shield override gizmos are shown.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldOverride_UsingGlobal: This shield uses the global shield style.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldOverride_UsingLocal: This shield has its own style. Rows set to "Follow global" still track the global settings.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldOverride_ReplacementO: This shield family's replacement is currently off, so these changes will not be visible until it is enabled on the Shields tab.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldOverride_FollowGlobal: Use whatever the Shields tab currently selects for this row.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldOverride_ColorOverrid: Uses a custom RGB tint for this shield instead of its def's color. Transparency still comes from the shield itself, so the picker's alpha is ignored.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldOverride_ColorSwatchT: Current shield color. Click "Choose color..." to change it.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_StyleCrispTip: A sharp ring that stops exactly on the intercept radius. Outline thickness and brightness are below.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_RidgeWidthTip: Half-width of the outline band in screen pixels; unchanged by zoom or shield size.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_RidgeBrightnessT: Brightness of the outline band. At 0 only the hot core and inner glow remain; use thickness to make it bolder.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexTip: Spherical hex/pentagon panels with flat per-cell shading, so it reads as half a sphere. The defaults are Hex wave for hits and Hex dissipate for breaks; both can be changed below.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_StyleVanillaTip: Imitates the stock textures: a narrow rim for domes, a soft bubble for belts.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_StyleBubbleTip: Uses the personal shield's soft bubble on a large shield.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_StyleHexBubbleTi: A shield bubble under a transparent hex net. It does not pulse: a feathered scan band reveals the net, and the whole net stays opaque for the hit and break animations. Its hit and break defaults are the hex wave and hex dissipate, shared with the hexagonal surface.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexBubbleScanPer: Seconds for one scan stripe to cross the shield. Shared by large shields and belts.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexBubbleFeather: Soft transition on both edges of the scan band. Band width is fixed at 0.06 and the leading-edge highlight at 0.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexBubbleStripes: Number of horizontal stripes sweeping at once, evenly spaced along the scan path.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexBubbleBaselin: Residual net visibility outside the scan band. 0 = the net is only visible where the band has passed.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexBubblePulseTi: On keeps vanilla's periodic brightness pulse. Off uses one fixed, lower opacity whose average brightness matches the pulsing original, so the shield stops flickering. Shared by both shield families.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexBubbleNote: Hex bubble reuses the line brightness, lattice density and bake controls below. Panel brightness has no effect on it (the net is transparent). The whole net stays opaque through hit and break, for exactly those animations' duration.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_VanillaNote: Vanilla-style and bubble styles use fixed proportions, with no outline sliders.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexFaceTip: Fill brightness of each panel; too high drowns the cell lines.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexLineTip: Strength of the bright line between panels; its width stays constant at any zoom.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexCenterClearTi: Brightness returns to full over this share of the radius, so pawns and buildings underneath show through. 0 disables it; 1 carries the gradient all the way to the rim. Only the static surface and net are affected; the rim, scan band, hit and break effects are not.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexDensityTip: Panels over the sphere grow with k: 2 ≈ 42, 5 ≈ 252, 12 ≈ 1442. The slider is a draft; press the button to bake it.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexPending: Showing k={0}; draft k={1}. Press the button above to bake (brief hitch).
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_ImpactFlareTip: Paints a wedge toward the incoming shot.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_ImpactBrightenTi: The shield brightens in the impact's angular sector, fading toward the centre.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_ImpactHexWaveTip: Panels near the impact light up and the light spreads outward through the lattice. Available on the hexagonal surface and the hex bubble.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_ImpactDurationTi: How long the flare, sector brightening or hex wave lasts on a large shield; 60 ticks = 1 second.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_FlareAlphaTip: Peak brightness of one interception; shared by Flare and Brighten sector.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_FlareSizeTip: Angular size multiplier for the flare; width still follows damage, capped at 45% of the shield radius.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_FlareDamageTip: How much hit brightness follows damage. 0 makes all weapons alike; higher makes heavy weapons stand out.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_BrightenAngleTip: Full width of the brighten sector, 30° in vanilla. Damage changes brightness, not the angle.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexImpactTip: Peak brightness of the panels lit by Hex wave.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_HexImpactReachTi: How far the light travels from the impact, as a share of the distance to the far rim.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_DisableHitDustTi: On removes dust when a large shield intercepts; the flash and sound remain.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_BreakVanillaTip: No custom animation: the shield vanishes at once, keeping vanilla's flash and sound.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_BreakDissolveTip: Erodes along a noise-driven tear with a hot edge and fine cracks.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_BreakHexDissipat: Loses panels one by one outward from the failure point. Available on the hexagonal surface and the hex bubble.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_DissolveTimeTip: Ticks from the first crack to fully gone; 60 ticks = 1 second.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_DissolveBrightne: Brightness as it breaks; vanilla visibility is already zero, so the animation carries its own.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_RestoreNoneTip: No animation: the shield appears at its normal size and opacity when it comes back online.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_RestoreFadeTip: The shield fades from transparent to its normal opacity when it comes back online.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_RestoreGrowTip: The shield fades in while expanding from a smaller size when it comes back online. Default.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_RestoreTimeTip: Ticks from the start of the restore to fully visible; 60 ticks = 1 second.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalHexDensi: Belts are much smaller than domes, so they use their own density. Default k=4, slightly sparser than the dome.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalHexPendi: Showing k={0}; draft k={1}. Press the button above to bake.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalOpacityT: Belts lack vanilla's pulsing alpha; the default 0.4 matches nearby shields.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalDisableH: On removes hit dust; the flash and sound remain.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalHitJitte: The bubble is pushed and shrinks when a hit is blocked, like vanilla.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalHitBrigh: The struck sector of the surface lights up.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalHitHexWa: Panels near the impact light up and spread outward.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalJitterDi: Maximum displacement in cells. Vanilla uses 0.05.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalBrighten: Full width of the sector. Vanilla uses 30°.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldDome_PersonalHitDurat: How long the effect lasts; 60 ticks = 1 second.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldRipple_Enable: Ripple when a hit is blocked
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldRipple_EnableTip: A ring spreads across the shield when it stops a shot or intercepts bombardment.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldRipple_IntensityTip: Baseline ripple strength; actual strength scales with damage. Too high and the ground looks torn.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldRipple_DurationTip: How long the ring lives; harder hits last longer.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_ShieldRipple_DamageScaleTip: How much damage drives ripple size. Lower is more uniform; higher makes heavy weapons stand out.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_EnableTip: Makes the view shimmer where the air is hot: hot rooms, fires, geothermal vents and heat-wave weather all trigger it. The hotter it gets, the stronger the distortion; ordinary warm weather stays subtle, while a fire or a heat wave clearly bends the scene.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_HighFrequencyTip: Off is cheaper. The shimmer lags a couple of seconds behind the temperature, which reads more like air slowly heating up. On, it appears as soon as a fire is lit, but costs more.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_PerCellTempTip: Off uses vanilla room temperature: every cell in a room shares one value, so the shimmer covers the room as a flat block with a hard edge at each wall. On samples Atmosphere Overhaul's per-cell field instead, so the shimmer follows the actual heat around fires, vents and walls, and a single room can have hot and cool spots. Per-cell sampling reads every cell, which costs more than the room walk, most visibly when zoomed far out.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_ShaderMissing: The heat-haze shader failed to load, so this option has no effect (see the log for details).
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_StartTempTip: Places at or below this temperature do not shimmer. The default 35 °C keeps ordinary comfortable rooms and temperate weather clear.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_FullTempTip: At or above this temperature the shimmer is at full strength, with a smooth transition in between. It is capped at 240 °C, so hotter air does not get any stronger.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_IntensityTip: How strong the distortion is. 1 is the recommended starting point; 0 still draws it, but with no visible movement.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_AmplitudeTip: How far the view shifts at full heat, in pixels. Keep it small: 2–4 px reads as hot air, while large values look like a warped lens.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_ScaleTip: Smaller values give fine, restless ripples; larger values give broad, slow waves. Around 1 roughly matches the size of a cell.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_SpeedTip: How fast the shimmer rises and changes. The lowest setting is only slower, never completely still.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Heat_FireBoostTip: Extra shimmer added directly around fires, campfires, heaters, torches and heat vents. Room temperature already includes indoor heat, so this mainly makes outdoor sources visible immediately. 0 turns the extra effect off.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Cold_EnableTip: Floats slow vapour in cold indoor air: freezers, ice-sheet bases, and any room kept cool by coolers. The haze curls and thickens in place instead of drifting across the map. It only appears inside real rooms and never outdoors; open rooms missing more than a quarter of their roof count as outdoors and are skipped too. Vanilla's vacuum fog and Atmosphere Overhaul's mist are both unaffected.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Cold_ShaderMissing: The cold-mist shader failed to load, so this option has no effect (see the log for details).
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Cold_StartTempTip: Rooms at or above this temperature stay completely clear. The default 0 °C keeps ordinary comfortable rooms and temperate bases clean, so only real freezers show any haze.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Cold_FullTempTip: Rooms at or below this temperature get the thickest haze, with a smooth transition in between. The default -75 °C leaves an ordinary freezer (around -18 °C) at roughly a quarter strength and reserves full strength for deep ice-sheet cold rooms.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Cold_OpacityTip: Maximum opacity where the haze is thickest. The default 0.1 is a thin veil; it is easy to overdo, and above 0.3 it visibly smears the floor and the items on it.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Cold_CoverageTip: How much of a cold room is covered by mist. 0 leaves it basically clear; higher values cover more; 1 fills the whole room. If you can barely see the effect, raise this before raising opacity.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Cold_ScaleTip: Size of the vapour patches. Lower values give fine, restless wisps; higher values give broad banks that read as ground fog. Around 1 roughly matches the size of a cell.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Cold_SpeedTip: How fast the vapour curls, thickens and dissolves in place. The haze never slides across the screen as a whole; higher values make it churn more visibly.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Leak_EnableTip: On Odyssey vacuum maps, shows air escaping: a pale stream flows toward every open door, running vent or unpowered vacuum barrier that leads to a drier room, and hull demolition adds a short burst blowing out into space. The stream strength follows the real pressure difference and the air left in the room, and it fades out as vanilla's vacuum fog takes over; vanilla's fog itself is untouched.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Leak_ShaderMissing: The vacuum-leak shader failed to load, so this option has no effect (see the log for details).
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Leak_IntensityTip: How visible the airflow is overall. The default 1 is the recommended strength; lower is fainter, higher is more obvious. Each opening's strength still depends on the pressure difference; this only sets how visible the result is.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Leak_SpeedTip: How fast the streaks scroll along the flow. It changes only the motion, not strength, width or duration. It still freezes when paused, and dragging the slider never makes the pattern jump.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Leak_DurationScaleTip: How long one-off effects such as wall bursts and ceiling suction last. It changes only the duration, not strength, width or scroll speed. Door and vent streams follow the room's actual vacuum, so they are unaffected.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Leak_DistortionTip: Gently bends the scene behind the airflow, so the stream reads as moving air instead of a flat overlay. Off skips the bending entirely; a strength of 0 looks the same.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Leak_DistortionStrengthTip: Maximum bend in screen pixels where the stream is fully visible. Fainter parts of the stream bend less.
LanguageData.VisualTweaks_Leak_TraceTip: Only for developer troubleshooting. When on, it writes a lot of log lines, so keep it off during normal play.
